t.4.39.1: Then King Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, whose purpose had been accomplished, spoke to Rāma, tiger among men, crusher of enemy forces.
t.4.39.2: The mighty lords of the monkeys, who can take any form at will and shine like great Indra, all those who dwell in my realm, have come and are encamped here.
t.4.39.3: These fierce monkeys, resembling Daityas and Dānavas, have come here together with many thousands of monkeys of terrible valour.
t.4.39.4: They are renowned for their deeds and exploits, mighty, and have conquered weariness; famed for their valour, they are the foremost in resolute undertakings.
t.4.39.5: O Rāma, these vānaras, your servants, who roam the earth and the waters and dwell on many different mountains, have arrived here by tens of millions.
t.4.39.6: All of them abide by your command, all are devoted to the welfare of their elder; they will be able to accomplish what you desire, O subduer of enemies.
t.4.39.7: O tiger among men, let whatever you consider fitting for the moment be spoken. That army stands ready under your control, and it is for you to command it.
t.4.39.9: Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, embraced Sugrīva, who was speaking thus, with both his arms and spoke these words.
t.4.39.8: Admittedly, this task of theirs is known to me in truth; even so, you should command them as the matter truly stands.
t.4.39.10: Let it be found out, gentle one, whether Vaidehī is alive or not, and let that land in which Rāvaṇa dwells also be discovered, O greatly wise one.
t.4.39.11: And having found Vaidehī and the abode of Rāvaṇa, I shall then, at that time, together with you, do what the occasion demands.
t.4.39.12: I am not the master in this undertaking, O lord of the monkeys, nor is Lakṣmaṇa. You, O lord of the leaping monkeys, are both the cause of this undertaking and its master.
t.4.39.13: You yourself, O lord, command me what my task is to be, for you know what must be done by me, O hero; of this there is no doubt.
t.4.39.15: Thus addressed, Sugrīva, in the presence of Rāma and of the wise Lakṣmaṇa, spoke to the troop-leader named Vinata, a mighty lord of monkeys who resembled a mountain and whose roar was like the thunder of clouds.
t.4.39.14: Accompanied by friends, valiant, wise and knowing the right moment for things, you are devoted to our welfare; you have accomplished your purpose well and are the foremost of those who understand what is to be gained.
t.4.39.17: Surrounded by a hundred thousand swift and mighty monkeys, go to the eastern quarter with its mountains, woods and forests.
t.4.39.16: O best of monkeys, together with the monkeys born of Soma and Sūrya, you are equipped with sound judgment of place, time and policy in determining what ought and ought not to be done.
t.4.39.18: There, search for Sītā, the princess of Videha, and for the abode of Rāvaṇa, among the mountain fastnesses, in the forests, and along the rivers.
t.4.39.19: The lovely river Bhāgīrathī, the Sarayū and likewise the Kauśikī, the charming Yamunā, daughter of Kalinda, and the great mountain Yāmuna.
t.4.39.20: Search the Sarasvatī and the Sindhu, the Śoṇa whose waters gleam like jewels, the Mahī, and the Kālamahī, adorned with mountains and forests.
t.4.39.21: Search through the Brahmamālas and the Videhas, the Mālavas, the Kāśis and Kosalas, the Māgadhas and the great villages, the Puṇḍras and likewise the Vaṅgas.
t.4.39.22: The city of the silk-weavers and the land rich in silver mines: all this must be searched thoroughly by you as you hunt here and there.
t.4.39.24: And those who have taken refuge on the long-stretching peak of Mandara, the Karṇaprāvaraṇas, and likewise the Oṣṭhakarṇakas as well.
t.4.39.23: Seek Sītā, the beloved wife of Rāma and daughter-in-law of Daśaratha, and search too the mountains and the towns that reach into the ocean.
t.4.39.25: There are the fearsome Lohamukhas and the swift Ekapādakas, and imperishable, mighty men who devour men.
t.4.39.27: There are fearsome creatures that move beneath the waters, known as man-tigers; O forest-dwellers, all their dwelling places must be searched.
t.4.39.26: There dwell the Kirātas with tufts of hair over their ears, golden-limbed and pleasing to behold, and there too are the island-dwelling Kirātas who eat raw fish.
t.4.39.28: Search also the lands that are reached over mountains, by leaping and by boat, and Yavadvīpa, rich in jewels and adorned with seven kingdoms.
t.4.39.29: Having crossed beyond Suvarṇarūpyaka and Yavadvīpa, which is adorned with gold mines, one comes to the mountain named Śiśira.
t.4.39.30: Frequented by gods and Dānavas, it touches the sky with its peak. In the mountain fastnesses, the precipices and the forests of these mountains…
t.4.39.31: Rāvaṇa, together with Vaidehī, must be searched for here and there. Then you should look upon the most fearsome islands of the ocean as well.
t.4.39.32: There huge-bodied asuras, permitted by Brahmā and hungry for a long time, constantly seize shadows.
t.4.39.33: Having approached by a proper crossing-place that great ocean, which resembled a dark storm-cloud, was frequented by great serpents and roared with a mighty sound,
t.4.39.34: Then, having gone on, you will see the terrible ocean named Lohita, whose waters are red, and there too you will see that huge Kūṭaśālmalī tree.
t.4.39.36: There, demons called the Mandehas, mountain-like and dreadful, of many forms and inspiring terror, hang from the mountain peaks.
t.4.39.35: There, too, you will see the dwelling of Vainateya, adorned with many kinds of jewels, resembling Kailāsa, built by Viśvakarman.
t.4.39.38: Then, having gone onward, O invincible ones, you will behold the ocean named Kṣīroda, resembling a pale white cloud, its waves making it look like a necklace of pearls.
t.4.39.37: Every day, at the rising of the sun, they fall into the water, and, scorched by the sun, they hang there again and again.
t.4.39.39: In its midst stands a very white mountain named Ṛṣabha, surrounded by blossoming trees of heavenly fragrance and by silvery trees.
t.4.39.40: And there is a lake, Sudarśana by name, filled with silver lotuses that blaze with golden filaments and crowded with royal swans.
t.4.39.41: The gods, Cāraṇas, Yakṣas and Kiṃnaras, together with hosts of Apsarases, joyfully approach that lotus pond, eager for pleasure.
t.4.39.42: Having crossed the Ocean of Milk, O monkeys, you will then see Jaloda, the best of seas, which brings terror to all beings.
t.4.39.44: There is heard the cry of the creatures dwelling in the ocean, who wail aloud in their helplessness upon seeing that Vaḍavāmukha.
t.4.39.43: There that great fiery energy born of wrath was fashioned into the mighty Horse-Face; they say that its food, seized with tremendous force, is the whole world with all that moves and does not move.
t.4.39.45: In the region north of the Sea of Sweet Water, thirteen yojanas away, stands a great golden mountain named Jātarūpaśila.
t.4.39.46: The thousand-headed god Ananta, clad in blue garments, seated on the summit of the mountain and revered by all beings.
t.4.39.47: The golden, three-crested palm-tree banner of that great-souled one, set up on the summit of the mountain, shines resplendent together with its platform.
t.4.39.48: In the eastern quarter that structure was fashioned by the lords of the gods. Beyond it lies the glorious golden mountain Udaya.
t.4.39.49: Its peak, touching the sky and stretching a hundred yojanas, golden and divine, shines splendidly together with its terraced platform.
t.4.39.51: There stands a peak named Saumanasa, a yojana in breadth and rising ten yojanas high, made of gold and firmly fixed.
t.4.39.50: It shines with sāla, tāla and tamāla trees, and with flowering karṇikāras, divine, made of gold and radiant as the sun.
t.4.39.52: There, long ago, at the time of his three strides, Viṣṇu, the Supreme Person, placed his first step, and he made the summit of Meru his second.
t.4.39.54: There the great sages called Vaikhānasas and Vālakhilyas, ascetics with the color of the sun, are seen shining.
t.4.39.53: Having circled Jambūdvīpa by the northern way, the sun becomes visible there; that peak, of mighty elevation, is the loftiest of all.
t.4.39.56: In the thickets, caves and forests of that mountain, Rāvaṇa together with Vaidehī must be searched for here and there.
t.4.39.55: This is the island Sudarśana, whose eastern front shines brightly, and in which dwell the radiance and the sight of all living beings.
t.4.39.57: Pervaded by the radiance of the golden mountain and of the great-souled Sūrya, the eastern twilight shines forth red.
t.4.39.59: On all those mountains, in the caves and in the forests, and in those regions too which have not been named by me, Jānakī must be searched for.
t.4.39.58: Beyond that lies the farthest limit one may reach in the eastern quarter, which is thronged by the gods. It is devoid of moon and sun, invisible, and shrouded in darkness.
t.4.39.60: O bulls among monkeys, only this far is it possible for monkeys to go; what lies beyond that, sunless and boundless, we do not know.
t.4.39.61: Having found Vaidehī and the dwelling of Rāvaṇa, and having reached the Udaya mountain, return when the month is complete.
t.4.39.62: No one is to stay beyond a month; whoever stays longer shall be put to death by me. Having found Maithilī, return with your purpose accomplished.
t.4.39.63: O vānaras, having thoroughly searched the eastern quarter, beloved of the great Indra and adorned with clusters of forests, and having found Sītā, the beloved of the scion of the Raghu dynasty, you will then return and be happy.
